title: §3/§4 — unfinished member blocks convergence; gates emit real disposition
goal: Suppress cycle convergence when any iteration member's disposition satisfies disposition_unfinished (§4/A), route router-terminated reason through router_reason_disposition in spec-coverage/spec-correspondence/review-report instead of hardcoding 'complete' (§3/B), and amend ADR-063 to Accepted on #2187's vocabulary (§C).

steps.description: Write the red tests for §4/A — must fail at merge-base before the engine fix. New integration test file with three cases keyed on disposition words: T1 — design_verify_cycle fixture where design returns disposition:timed_out with structurally valid design.md, design-gate passes, spec-coverage is covered → cycle does NOT converge on that iteration (red: converges today). T2 — same fixture with disposition:complete → cycle DOES converge (positive baseline, must stay green). T3 — at max_iterations with the last iteration member having disposition:timed_out → cycle takes the existing exhaustion path, not complete. Reference construction pattern from tests/integration/cycle-multi-iter-cumulative-test.sh (stubbed verdicts_blob, no live LLM).

Engine fix for §4/A in cycle-orchestrator.sh. After the build-specific convergence suppression block (lines ~2575-2581, which fires when disposition_unfinished "$_build_disposition"), add a second generic suppression block: if converged==0 AND _iter_did_not_finish==1 then set converged=1 and emit cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence with iter/disposition context. The guard converged==0 prevents double-fire for an unfinished build (build-specific block already set converged=1). The _iter_did_not_finish variable is already computed at ~2541-2548 from ALL members via disposition_unfinished. Update the comment above _iter_did_not_finish to note it is now used for both the reason-aware exhaustion halt and convergence suppression.

Write the red tests for §3/B — must fail at merge-base before the plugin fixes. Three additions: (1) tests/unit/spec-coverage-test.sh — add SPEC-9: when route_to_model exits non-zero (stubbed rc), result has disposition:timed_out not 'complete'. (2) tests/unit/spec-correspondence-test.sh — add a parallel case: router timeout yields disposition from router_reason_disposition, not 'complete'. (3) tests/unit/review-report-v2-contract-test.sh — add a case: when a lens rc file holds a non-zero router exit code, the stage's result disposition is the router_reason_disposition of that code, not 'complete'. All three must fail before the corresponding plugin fixes.

Fix spec-coverage for §3/B. In spec_coverage_run (~line 187), replace '|| true' with an rc-capture pattern: run route_to_model in a subshell that writes the rc to a temp file, then read it back in the parent. Add an optional disposition parameter to _scv_write (default 'complete'). In the no-parseable-verdict branch (~line 201), when rc is non-zero, classify via _router_rc_classify + router_reason_disposition and pass the resulting disposition word to _scv_write instead of the hardcoded 'complete'. Reference implementation: plugins/agent/review-lens/plugin.sh (similar rc-capture + router_reason_disposition pattern).

Fix spec-correspondence for §3/B. In _sc_call (~line 121), the route_to_model call uses '|| true'; replace with rc capture to a temp file (a nameref cannot cross the command-substitution subshell boundary, so the temp-file pattern is required). Add an optional disposition parameter to _sc_write_result (default 'complete'). In spec_correspondence_run, pass a temp file path to _sc_call, read back the rc after the call, classify via _router_rc_classify + router_reason_disposition, and forward the disposition to _sc_write_result when rc is non-zero. Clean up the temp file after reading.

Fix review-report for §3/B. In the failed-lens loop (~lines 167-171), track the first non-zero rc seen across all failed lenses by reading per-lens .rc files alongside the existing verdict reads. After the loop, when _rr_failed_lenses is non-empty and a non-zero rc was recorded, classify it via _router_rc_classify + router_reason_disposition to get the disposition word; pass that to _rr_write_v2 instead of the hardcoded 'complete' at ~line 174. _rr_write_v2 already accepts disposition as its third positional argument; no signature change needed.

Amend ADR-063 (§C). Change Status to 'Accepted, amended 2026-10-05 by #2032'. In §3: replace every instance of 'exhausted' with 'timed_out'/'out_of_turns', note the classifier is router_reason_disposition (scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh:259), and add that 'complete' must never be hardcoded for a model-calling stage. In §4: strike 'exhausted → escalate' (retry + router-side timeout growth via ADR-029/route.sh replace it); keep and update the gate-fail-closed rule noting it is now implemented. In §1: replace 'one shared helper' with 'per-stage _<stage>_budget_guidance helpers each reading the enforcing values'. Add dated back-pointer to #2187.

notes:
ORDERING: Steps 1 and 3 (red tests) must be committed and confirmed failing before their corresponding implementation steps (2 and 4-6) per TDD discipline in CLAUDE.md and the issue's acceptance criteria. The PR body must state the assertion and how it failed at the merge-base.

CYCLE-ORCHESTRATOR INSERTION POINT (step 2): The build-specific suppression block ends with a 'fi' at approximately line 2581. The new generic block goes immediately after that fi, before the comment block introducing the no-committed-changes guard (~line 2583). Confirmed by code read: _iter_did_not_finish is computed at ~2541-2548 from ALL members via disposition_unfinished. If the build is unfinished, both the build-specific check (sets converged=1) and the generic check (converged==0 guard fails) would fire — harmless, build-specific wins. The empty_diff resting point is safe: it sets all members' dispositions to 'complete', so disposition_unfinished returns false, _iter_did_not_finish stays 0, and the generic check does not fire.

SPEC-CORRESPONDENCE RC CAPTURE (step 5): _sc_call's output is captured via command substitution (stdout is the raw model reply). Shell semantics prevent a nameref from crossing the subshell boundary. A temp file written inside the subshell and read by the parent is the correct mechanism, matching the approach used in review-lens and other similar stages.

REVIEW-REPORT WORST-RC (step 6): The .rc files per lens store raw router exit codes. 'First non-zero found' is sufficient — all non-zero codes classify to some unfinished disposition via router_reason_disposition. _rr_write_v2 already accepts disposition as its third positional argument; no signature change needed.

DESIGN-GATE NOT IN SCOPE: design-gate is a tool stage that did complete; it is design's timed_out disposition that suppresses convergence, and the engine fix (step 2) handles that. The fix is keyed on the disposition word, not the stage name.

BLOCKED-ON CONTEXT: This plan does NOT touch plan or impact (blocked on #1835/#1838). It only fixes spec-coverage, spec-correspondence, and review-report, all of which are already on result_contract v2. The ADR amendment documents the per-stage helper pattern but does not add new budget-block helpers to remaining stages (#2222's scope).

ALL FILES VERIFIED: cycle-orchestrator.sh, ADR-063.md, review-report/plugin.sh, spec-correspondence/plugin.sh, spec-coverage/plugin.sh, and the three unit test files all verified to exist at their expected paths. tests/integration/cycle-member-unfinished-no-convergence-test.sh is net-new (does not exist yet). router_reason_disposition confirmed at scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh:259.
